findings.title: Vendored fork default home is still ~/.hermes and is materialized at import time
findings.difference: The vendored fork's platform default is Path.home()/'.hermes' (unrebranded). Importing the vendored state store with QUBIT_HOME unset creates $HOME/.hermes as an import side effect. Qubit only guards this at the voicebridge.qubit_runtime.pin_qubit_home() boundary (qubit_runtime.py:226).
findings.observed: import qubit_state created <tmp>/.hermes (drwx------). On the operator host the same fallback targets the read-only /home/trick/.hermes when no guard runs.
findings.cause_type: unrebranded upstream default; guard is boundary-only, not global

findings.title: Runtime config toolsets references non-existent toolset 'Qubit-cli'
findings.qubit_file_line: runtime config.yaml:7 (live) ; qubit_runtime/toolsets.py:194 (only hermes-cli / lowercase qubit-cli alias)
findings.difference: Top-level toolsets is 'Qubit-cli' (capital Q). No toolset by that name exists. The lowercase alias registered by qubit_asgi.py:107 is 'qubit-cli', not 'Qubit-cli'.
findings.observed: Qubit-cli -> 0 tools; hermes-cli -> 53 tools. Active enablement uses platform 'cli'->'hermes-cli', so tools still load, but any surface reading top-level toolsets gets an empty bundle.
findings.cause_type: string-based reference failure: rebranded to a name never registered

findings.title: qubit gateway status is host-global, not QUBIT_HOME/profile scoped
